headline: Minnesota's 165-Mile Mesabi Trail Finally Complete After 30 Years
meta_description: One of America's longest paved bike trails officially opens in Minnesota, connecting 28 communities across the scenic Iron Range after three decades of work.
summary_short: After 30 years of planning and fundraising, Minnesota's 165-mile Mesabi Trail is now complete—one of the longest paved cycling paths in America.
body:
What began as a vision three decades ago has finally become reality: a 165-mile paved cycling trail now winds through Minnesota's Iron Range, connecting 28 communities from Grand Rapids to Ely and offering outdoor enthusiasts one of America's longest continuous routes. The Mesabi Trail, named after the historic iron ore mines that once fueled American industry during World War II, officially opened last Tuesday with a ribbon-cutting ceremony attended by a dozen officials. The trail's completion represents far more than infrastructure—it embodies a region's transformation. The shady woods and rolling hills that line the route were partly formed by decades-old heaps of earth from the mines themselves, now reclaimed with regrowing forests, turning industrial remnants into natural beauty.

The trail's creation required an unprecedented coalition of partners. The Department of Iron Range Resources & Rehabilitation—a unique state agency that reinvests mining profits into the community—provided crucial funding, but completion hinged on what IRRRB commissioner Ida Rukavina called "three decades of partnership and persistence." Along the route, travelers encounter far more than scenic vistas: historic buildings, mining artifacts, and markers of the region's ethnic and cultural heritage tell the story of the communities the trail passes through.

Already, tens of thousands of people use the trail annually, with visitors consistently awarding it five-star ratings. Whether biking, hiking, inline skating, or cross-country skiing, users find themselves never far from campgrounds, parks, and local services—food, lodging, fishing, canoeing, and golfing all accessible from nearby communities. The trail's official website helps visitors plan trips and connect with volunteer caretaker opportunities, ensuring this hard-won achievement continues to benefit the region for generations.
quick_facts: 165-mile paved cycling trail completed in Minnesota
Connects 28 communities from Grand Rapids to Ely
Named after historic Mesabi Range iron ore mines
Took over 30 years of planning, construction, and fundraising
Already attracts tens of thousands of annual users
